INTEGRATED SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Paper burning to ash

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.

9. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

11. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.

13. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.

15. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

16. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
